fields.title: Valuation Judgment — Probability-Weighted Assumed Value · Price Decomposition · Judgment-Change Triggers
fields.md:
(Only the public items of the master's four stages are included — assumed value, price decomposition, triggers.)

### Probability-Weighted Assumed Value
- Discount rate 9.2% = risk-free 4.95% (US 10-year, data/latest.json meta.macro.ust10, 2026-11-03) + ERP 5.0% × beta 0.85 (assumption). 10-year discount factor 2.411 (formula 1.092^10).
- Present value = 2036 BPS × exit P/B ÷ 2.411: bull $684.5 · base $464.4 · bear $265.0 → probability-weighted $469.6 (formula).
- Assumed value band $265.0–$684.5, midpoint (base) $464.4. The current B share price of $570.89 (2026-11-06 close, [stockanalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/brk.b/statistics/)) is 23% above the base scenario (570.89 ÷ 464.4 − 1, formula).
- Cross-check (two-bucket method, calculation): investment assets per share (net cash $356.946 billion + equities $335.515 billion) ÷ 2.12835 billion B-share equivalents = $325.4; annualized after-tax operating earnings excluding investment income $38.08 billion (9M 28,562 × 4/3) ÷ 0.79 = pre-tax $48.2 billion → $22.65 per share × 10 = $226.5 → total $551.8. By this method the gap to the share price is 4% (formula; sources are the 3Q26 10-Q and press release). The difference between the two methods comes from the assumptions of an 'exit P/B of 1.45x' versus '10x pre-tax earnings'.
- Sensitivity: lowering the discount rate by 1 percentage point to 8.2% raises the base-scenario present value to about $509 (formula 464.4 × 2.411 ÷ 2.199); raising BPS compounding to 9% also gives about $509 (formula 357.73 × 2.367 × 1.45 ÷ 2.411).

### What Is and Isn't Reflected in the Price
- Reverse calculation: holding the exit P/B fixed at 1.45x, the current price reflects BPS compounding of 10.25% per year (formula (570.89 × 2.411 ÷ (357.73 × 1.45))^(1/10) − 1). If the current P/B of 1.60x is assumed to persist, it is 9.17% (same formula).
- Value of the cash pile: market cap $1,215.1 billion − net cash $356.9 billion − equities $335.5 billion = about $522.6 billion that the market assigns to the operating subsidiaries and insurance underwriting business → 13.7 times annualized after-tax operating earnings excluding investment income of $38.08 billion (formula; an approximation ignoring deferred taxes and float liabilities). This means the market is valuing cash 1:1 without a discount.
- Buffett premium/discount: no discount is observed right after the succession — B shares are up 14.6% since the end of September (497.95 → 570.89, formula; 9/30 close sourced from [24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/05/berkshire-has-gained-16-in-about-5-weeks/) 2026-11-05), reportedly outpacing the S&P 500 by more than 18 percentage points over the same period ([Reuters republication](https://gvwire.com/2026/11/07/berkshire-hathaway-accelerates-stock-buybacks-operating-profit-falls/)). This is mixed with a shift by the market from high-valuation AI assets toward a 'defensive compounding machine' (judgment).
- Not reflected (possibilities): earnings leverage if the cash is deployed on a large scale (bull side), and lower investment income from falling interest rates (bear side).
